comparison: Perfect agreement on the correlation between motor and visual biases (C72, C73). Both evaluations find this evidence convincing and supportive of a shared underlying mechanism, though OpenEval notes the mechanistic claim is inferential rather than directly demonstrated.

Perfect agreement on learning analysis (C74-C81). Both evaluations support the finding of no learning effects across sessions. This analysis directly addressed a peer reviewer question and strengthens the main findings by ruling out practice effects.

Both address AQ validity and limitations (C119-C128), but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, expressing stronger concerns about generalizability to clinical ASD and gender bias in the AQ measure.

Strong agreement on motor updating findings (C54-C61, C84-C91). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing with appropriate controls. Peer review includes additional claims C6, C7 not in OpenEval result. Both emphasize the importance of control analyses showing intact first saccades.

Strong agreement on visual updating findings (C62-C71, C102-C104, C107). Both evaluations find statistical evidence robust and controls appropriate. Peer review includes additional claims C8, C9, C10, C116, C117 not grouped in OpenEval R2. Both emphasize ruling out alternative explanations.

Both address integrative conclusions about efference copy dysfunction (C82, C83, C105, C106, C108, C112, C129, C130). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic claims are speculative. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing concerns about linking findings to actual ASD symptoms and sensory/motor difficulties.

Partial overlap on alternative explanations. OpenEval R6 addresses dimensional specificity and memory demands (C92-C95) as SUPPORTED. Peer R5 addresses the same claims as SUPPORTED, noting these analyses responded to reviewer concerns about memory demands.

Both address the visual cue limitation (C96, C97). OpenEval rates overall result as SUPPORTED while acknowledging this caveat. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 explicitly concerned that allocentric cues could provide an alternative explanation that was not definitively ruled out.

OpenEval evaluates methodological approach and sample characteristics (C49-C51, C119, C133-C139) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these methodological claims, though C119 appears in peer R8 focused on AQ validity.

OpenEval evaluates background and theoretical motivation (C1-C5, C11-C19) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these represent literature review and rationale rather than novel findings.

OpenEval evaluates neurophysiological background on efference copy (C20-C33) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these represent established literature and study hypotheses rather than results.

OpenEval evaluates theoretical discussion of competing views (C34-C43) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature of proposed resolution and connection to autism. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these theoretical claims.

OpenEval evaluates description of established paradigms and hypotheses (C44-C48, C52-C53) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these represent methodological background and a priori predictions.

OpenEval evaluates discussion contextualizing findings within broader literature (C98-C101, C109-C114) as SUPPORTED, though noting mechanistic connections are speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these discussion claims.

OpenEval evaluates concluding statements (C131, C132) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these represent summary and future directions rather than specific findings requiring peer evaluation.
